title: From UX to CEO: how Designers are taking on leadership roles in companies
description: Why UX Designers have an edge in leadership roles, and a step-by-step path to grow from designer to Head, CPO or CEO.

related.title: Clint Scale
related.body: In practice: an explorable design system, with tokens, components, contrast and governance.

blocks.text: For a long time, designers were seen as “the screen people,” responsible only for pretty, intuitive interfaces. But that has changed. Today, many tech leaders started their careers as UX Designers and kept taking on strategic roles until they reached the top of the corporate ladder.
The question is: how does that transition happen?

If you want to expand your influence, shape big decisions and even hold a leadership position, whether as Head of Design, CPO (Chief Product Officer) or even CEO, you need to understand what sets apart the designers who make this journey from those who stay stuck in visual design. Let's explore the paths for this growth and how you can map that route in your career.
Why do UX Designers have an edge in leadership?

Leadership takes a mix of strategic vision, analytical skills and communication. UX Designers naturally build some of these qualities over their careers. Here are three reasons designers are landing prominent positions in companies:

items.title: Moves across teams
items.body: A systemic view of the product.

blocks.caption: Three advantages designers already build in practice.

items: User-centered thinking: Great leaders deeply understand their customers. UX Designers have this mindset from day one, which makes it easier to create products and strategies truly aligned with market needs.
Data-driven decision making: UX practice already involves analyzing metrics, A/B testing and user research. That data-driven mindset is a big differentiator for any executive.

Ability to move across teams: Designers constantly work with developers, product managers, marketing and stakeholders. That cross-functional work helps build a systemic view, essential for senior leaders.

blocks.text: But knowing this isn't enough. The question is: how do you step out of design and into the leadership game?
Step by step for UX Designers who want to become leaders

data.title: Every floor asks for a new skill

floors.skill: Work closely with PMs, CPOs and CEOs
Learn to communicate ideas with impact
Step out of your comfort zone and take on bigger responsibilities

blocks.text: 1. Build management and leadership skills

blocks.caption: The path this article describes: each step asks for more business vision.

blocks.text: Being an excellent designer isn't enough to take on a leadership role.

items: Start by leading small projects inside the company.
Learn about team management, company culture and leadership methods.
Ask for feedback on your management skills and keep working on them.

blocks.text: 2. Expand your view beyond design
UX Designers who grow into leadership roles don't just think about screens, they think about product and strategy.

items: Understand how the business works financially (CAC, LTV, ROI, retention, churn).
Study product strategy and how UX decisions affect company growth.
Develop a critical eye for the market and the competition.

blocks.text: 3. Work closely with PMs, CPOs and CEOs
Internal networking is essential. Leaders aren't made alone: they need to understand and connect with the people already making big decisions.

items: Join strategic meetings and understand the logic behind executive decisions.
Bring valuable business insights based on user behavior.
Position yourself as a strategic partner, not just someone who executes requests.

blocks.text: 4. Learn to communicate ideas with impact
A great leader needs to sell their ideas clearly and persuasively. To do that:

items: Sharpen your storytelling and presentation skills.
Use data and insights to back your proposals with solid grounding.
Become an excellent communicator, able to align different teams and stakeholders.

blocks.text: 5. Step out of your comfort zone and take on bigger responsibilities
If you want to grow, you have to be willing to leave the design bubble and accept challenges outside your traditional area.

items: Take on projects involving strategy, innovation and high-impact decisions.
Explore other areas like business, growth and marketing.
Show initiative to solve problems and improve processes at the company.

blocks.text: Success stories: Designers who made it to the top
Several tech leaders started their careers in design and now hold strategic positions at some of the biggest companies in the world. A few examples:

items.body: From designer to CPO at Adobe.

items.body: Trained as a designer, CEO of Airbnb.

items.body: Former VP of Design at Facebook.

items: Scott Belsky: Started as a designer and became Chief Product Officer at Adobe.
Brian Chesky: Trained as a designer, today he's CEO and co-founder of Airbnb.
Julie Zhuo: Former VP of Design at Facebook, directly shaping the company's strategy.
data.close: What do these leaders have in common? They went beyond design and became product and business strategists.

blocks.text: Conclusion: The future of UX Designers is strategic

The new generation of designers needs to go beyond interfaces and think more broadly. If you want to grow in your career and hold a leadership position, the path is open, but it takes effort, continuous learning and strategic vision.
The market values designers who think like leaders. The question is: are you ready to take that step?
